mainTopic: Selling animals to a גוי: the worry of רביעה, and the ban on selling large animals because of work on שבת (renting, lending and testing)
overview: The amud opens with רבי אלעזר: even where it is forbidden to leave an animal alone with a גוי, selling one to him is allowed, because a גוי protects his own animal so it will not become sterile. The גמרא adds that רב also changed his mind and agreed. It then explains the משנה's rule that large animals may never be sold to a גוי. The reason is not רביעה but the worry that the animal will be worked on שבת. The first answer is a גזירה because of lending and renting, but that is challenged on the grounds that a renter or borrower also 'acquires' the animal. רמי בריה דרב ייבא offers a new reason, 'testing': a Jew selling near sunset on ערב שבת might drive his own animal with his voice on שבת. Two אמוראים then question whether renting gives ownership, and the case of a כהן renting a cow proves that it does not. So the ban rests on all three concerns: renting, lending and testing. The amud ends with practical cases: רב אדא allows selling a donkey through a middleman, and רב הונא sells a cow, saying the buyer may want it for slaughter.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר permits selling an animal even where leaving it alone is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that selling an animal to a גוי is allowed even in a place where it is forbidden to leave one's animal alone with a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר says: even in a place where they forbade leaving an animal alone with a גוי, it is allowed to sell it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opinion of רבי אלעזר. He separates two things: leaving an animal alone with a גוי, and selling an animal to a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving an animal alone (ייחוד) with a גוי can be forbidden because of the worry of רביעה. רבי אלעזר says this worry does not stretch to selling. Even where ייחוד is banned, a sale is still permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: To leave an animal alone (in seclusion) with a גוי

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:
Even in a place where they forbade leaving an animal alone with a gentile,
it is permitted to sell it to him.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling an animal to a גוי is permitted even where ייחוד with a גוי is forbidden.

steps.title: What is the reason for רבי אלעזר's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר allows selling when ייחוד is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אלעזר's ruling. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we worry about רביעה when an animal is left alone with a גוי, it seems we should worry even more once the גוי owns it. The question asks what makes a sale different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a sale is allowed when ייחוד is not.

steps.title: A gentile protects his own animal from becoming sterile
steps.stepSummary: A גוי will not do רביעה with his own animal, because it could make the animal sterile.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גוי takes care of his own animal so that it will not become sterile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: once the animal belongs to the גוי, he protects it. He does not want to damage his own property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry of רביעה applies to someone else's animal, which the גוי does not care about. Once he owns it, his own interest keeps him away, because רביעה could make it sterile. That is why a sale is fine even where ייחוד is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes care of (spares) his own animal

phrases.english: A gentile spares his own animal
so that it will not become sterile.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוֹי חָס עַל בְּהֶמְתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא תֵּעָקֵר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גוי protects his own animal from רביעה so it will not become sterile, so there is no worry once it is his.

steps.title: רב also changed his mind and agreed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב retracted his opinion and accepted the same reasoning, as quoted in his name by רב שילא בר אבימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רב retracted. For רב תחליפא said in the name of רב שילא בר אבימי, quoting רב: a גוי spares his own animal so it will not become sterile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that רב, who had held otherwise, came around to רבי אלעזר's view. It backs this up with a quote in רב's name using the very same reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "even רב retracted" tell us רב once held that selling was forbidden wherever ייחוד was forbidden. A chain of transmitters now quotes רב himself giving the reason 'a גוי spares his own animal.' This shows he later agreed that a sale is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי אלעזר and (in the end) רב hold that selling an animal to a גוי is not a problem of רביעה, because a גוי protects his own animal.

phrases.english: And even Rav retracted his opinion,
as Rav Taḥlifa says

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁילָא בַּר אֲבִימִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Sheila bar Avimi says in the name of Rav:
A gentile spares his own animal
so that it will not become sterile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב also accepted the reasoning of step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב retracted and agreed that a גוי spares his own animal, so a sale is allowed.

steps.title: Why may large animals never be sold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that large livestock may not be sold to a גוי anywhere, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but in every place one may not sell large livestock, etc. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה: large animals may not be sold to a גוי in any place. It asks why, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the worry of רביעה does not block a sale. So the ban on selling large animals 'in every place' needs a different reason, and the גמרא asks what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: In every place (no matter the local custom)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume this ban is about רביעה. The גמרא just said that worry does not apply to a sale. The reason here is something else.

phrases.english: But in every place one may not sell
large livestock, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." points to the rest of the משנה line, which also lists calves and foals, whole or injured.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְכׇל מָקוֹם אֵין מוֹכְרִין בְּהֵמָה גַּסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the total ban on selling large animals to a גוי.

steps.title: The worry is that the animal will be made to work
steps.stepSummary: We are not worried about רביעה, but we are worried the גוי will make the animal do work (on שבת).
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, we are not worried about רביעה. But we are worried that he will make it do work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ban on large animals is about מלאכה (work), not רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Large animals are work animals. The concern is that the animal will do מלאכה on שבת, and a Jew is commanded about his animal resting on שבת. This step names the worry; the next step asks why it should matter after a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: An improper relationship with an animal

phrases.english: Granted, we are not concerned about bestiality,
but we are concerned about him putting it to work.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is because of the worry that the animal will be worked on שבת.

steps.title: Once he bought it, it is his, so let him work it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: once the גוי bought the animal, it is fully his, so why care if he works it on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him work it! Since he bought it, he owns it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason just given. After a sale the animal no longer belongs to the Jew, so its work on שבת should not be the Jew's concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jew's duty about his animal resting on שבת only applies to an animal he owns. Once the sale is done, the גוי owns it completely. So the worry about work seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: So let him do (work with it)!

phrases.english: And let him put it to work!
Since he bought it, he has acquired it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the animal will be worked on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the sale the animal belongs to the גוי, so the Jew has no responsibility for its rest on שבת.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree because of lending and renting
steps.stepSummary: Selling is banned as a גזירה, so that people will not come to lend or rent their animals to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree because of lending and because of renting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a sale itself is no problem. The חכמים banned it so people would not come to lend or rent an animal to a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an animal is lent or rented, it still belongs to the Jew. If the גוי works it on שבת, the Jew's own animal is working. To keep people from those cases, the חכמים also forbade selling.

phrases.english: It is a decree because of lending
and because of renting.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: After a sale there is nothing wrong, so selling should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Selling is banned so people will not lend or rent, where the animal stays the Jew's.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic pattern: the חכמים forbid something allowed in itself, to protect against a similar case that really is a problem.

steps.title: A borrower and a renter also acquire the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: borrowing and renting also give the גוי a kind of ownership, so why is working it a problem?
steps.simpleTranslation: But borrowing it, he acquires it, and renting it, he acquires it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of the previous step. It argues that a borrower or renter also 'acquires' the animal for that time, so even those cases should be fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree only makes sense if lending and renting are really a problem. But a borrower or renter holds the animal for a set time. If that counts as acquiring it, the work on שבת is not the Jew's concern there either, and the decree has nothing to guard against.

phrases.english: Borrowing it, he acquires it,
phrases.notes: He means the borrower gets a kind of ownership for the time he holds it.

phrases.english: and renting it, he acquires it!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that lending and renting are a problem worth a decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A borrower and a renter also acquire the animal for that time, so its work on שבת would not be the Jew's responsibility there either.

steps.title: A new reason: the animal might be tested on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רמי בריה דרב ייבא says the sale was banned because of 'testing'. A sale near sunset on ערב שבת can lead the Jewish seller to drive his own animal on שבת, which carries a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רמי son of רב ייבא said: it is a גזירה because of testing. Sometimes a Jew sells the animal to a גוי close to sunset on Friday. The גוי says to him, 'Come, test it for me.' The animal hears the Jew's voice and walks because of him, and the Jew is glad that it walks. So he becomes someone who drives his animal on שבת, and someone who drives his animal on שבת is liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier answer (step 8) was knocked down in step 9. Now the גמרא gives a brand new reason why selling a large animal to a גוי is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer no longer depends on lending or renting at all. The worry is about the moment of the sale itself. Right before שבת, the Jew may show the buyer that the animal works, and the animal obeys its Jewish owner's voice. The Jew is then doing the איסור of driving his own animal on שבת, so the rabbis banned the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Testing, meaning trying out the animal to see that it works
Friday, the day going into שבת
Someone who drives an animal from behind with his voice or a stick
A sin-offering, brought for doing an איסור by mistake

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not what the גוי does. The problem is that the Jew himself makes his own animal walk on שבת by using his voice.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's rule without needing the 'renting gives ownership' idea that step 9 used to attack step 8.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rami son of Rav Yeiva said:
It is a decree because of testing,
for sometimes he sells it to him
close to sunset on Shabbat eve,
and he says to him: 'Come, test it for me,'
phrases.notes: The buyer wants the seller to show him that the animal really works.

phrases.english: and it hears his voice and walks because of him,
and he is pleased that it walks,
phrases.notes: The seller is happy because it proves to the buyer that the animal is a good worker.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ מְחַמֵּר אַחֵר בְּהֶמְתּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: and he becomes one who drives his animal on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמְחַמֵּר אַחֵר בְּהֶמְתּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת חַיָּיב חַטָּאת.
phrases.english: and one who drives his animal on Shabbat is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of step 8, which step 9 challenged, with a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New underlying reason for the גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the animal is sold it belongs to the גוי, so work done on it on שבת should not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The danger is at the sale near שבת. The Jew may drive his own animal while showing it to the buyer, so the rabbis forbade the sale.

steps.title: Does renting really give ownership? A proof from renting a house
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי questions the idea that renting gives ownership. A משנה forbids renting a house to a גוי as a home because he will bring עבודה זרה into it. If renting made it his house, why would that matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי objected: Does renting really give ownership? But we learned in a משנה: even in a place where they allowed renting houses to a גוי, they did not allow it for a living home, because he brings עבודה זרה into it. If you think renting gives ownership, then when he brings it in, he is bringing it into his own house!
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא attacks the assumption from step 9 that renting gives the renter a kind of ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 argued that a renter owns the animal for now, so his working it on שבת should not matter. רב שישא says that cannot be right. A משנה treats a rented house as still belonging to the Jew, since the Jew may not let idols come into it. If renting made it the גוי's house, there would be nothing wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it, a strong challenge

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi objected to it:
And does renting give ownership?
phrases.notes: He is going after the idea from step 9 that a renter owns the animal for now.

phrases.english: But we learned in a mishna:
Even in a place where they said one may rent
they did not say it for a residence,
because he brings idol worship into it.
And if it enters your mind that renting gives ownership,
when this one brings it in,
he is bringing it into his own house!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: וּשְׂכִירוּת מִי קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the assumption used in step 9 and challenges it from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in step 9 that renting gives the renter ownership
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If renting gave ownership, the rented house would count as the גוי's house. Then bringing עבודה זרה into it would not be forbidden. But the משנה forbids it.

steps.title: עבודה זרה is a special, stricter case
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside. עבודה זרה is extra strict because the פסוק says 'Do not bring an abomination into your house'. So the house case does not show that renting gives no ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: עבודה זרה is different because it is severe, as it is written: 'And you shall not bring an abomination into your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רב שישא's proof by saying the house case is special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if renting does give ownership, עבודה זרה is treated more strictly. The פסוק speaks of 'your house', and the house still carries the Jewish owner's name. So the משנה about houses cannot teach us a general rule about renting.

phrases.english: Idol worship is different, as it is severe,
as it is written: 'And you shall not bring an abomination into your house.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the house משנה. It does not decide whether renting gives ownership.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The house case involves עבודה זרה, which has its own extra strictness from a פסוק. So it cannot teach a general rule about renting.

steps.title: A second challenge: a rented cow and תרומה feed
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא again questions whether renting gives ownership. He brings a משנה about a rented cow: a כהן who rents a cow from a ישראל may not feed it תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק son of רב משרשיא objected: Does renting really give ownership? But we learned in a משנה: a ישראל who rented a cow from a כהן may feed it vetches of תרומה. And a כהן who rented a cow from a ישראל may not feed it vetches of תרומה, even though he is responsible for feeding it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא attacks the same idea from step 9, that renting gives ownership. This time he uses a case with no עבודה זרה, so the answer of step 12 cannot help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a כהן's animal may eat תרומה. The משנה follows the real owner, not the renter. A כהן renting a ישראל's cow may not feed it תרומה, even though he pays for its food. This shows that renting does not make the animal his.

keyTerms.meaning: Vetches, a bean-like plant used as animal feed
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which only a כהן and his household may eat

steps.whatToRemember: Two challenges were raised against 'renting gives ownership'. The house case was pushed aside because עבודה זרה is strict. The cow-and-תרומה case is a cleaner proof, since no עבודה זרה is involved.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Mesharshiyya objected to it:
And does renting give ownership?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
An Israelite who rented a cow from a priest
may feed it vetches of teruma,
and a priest who rented a cow from an Israelite,
even though feeding it is his responsibility,
may not feed it vetches of teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: וּשְׂכִירוּת מִי קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new proof against the same assumption, avoiding the 'עבודה זרה is strict' answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in step 9 that renting gives the renter ownership
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If renting gave ownership, a כהן who rents a cow would own it and could feed it תרומה. The משנה forbids this, so the cow is still the ישראל's.

steps.title: The rented cow proves that renting does not give ownership
steps.stepSummary: If renting gave ownership, the כהן could feed the rented cow תרומה, since it would count as his own cow. The משנה forbids it, so renting does not give ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think renting makes you the owner, why can't the כהן feed the cow תרומה? It would be his own cow! So we learn that renting does not make you the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof that רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא started in step 13. It shows that renting something does not make you its owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may feed תרומה to an animal that belongs to him. The משנה forbids feeding it to a cow he only rented, so a rented cow must still belong to the ישראל. That means renting does not transfer ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind (you might think)

steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the קשיא from step 9. If renting does not give ownership, then a rented animal still belongs to the Jew, and its working on שבת is his problem.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that renting acquires,
why may he not feed it?
It is his own cow!
Rather, learn from this
renting does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the argument from the משנה quoted in step 13.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that a כהן who rents a cow from a ישראל may not feed it תרומה

steps.title: The ban rests on renting, lending, and testing
steps.stepSummary: Since renting does not give ownership, the ban on selling large animals to a גוי is a decree made for three reasons: renting, lending, and testing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have said renting does not make you the owner, the ban is a decree because of renting, a decree because of lending, and a decree because of testing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the discussion. It lists all three reasons why the רבנן forbade selling a large animal to a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting and lending a Jew's animal to a גוי would leave the animal still his, so it would be working for him on שבת. Testing is the sunset-sale worry from step 10. All three concerns now stand together as the basis of the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree, a protective ban
Testing (the buyer trying out the animal)
And now that you have said

steps.whatToRemember: Renting does not give ownership. The ban on selling large animals to a גוי rests on three concerns: renting, lending, and testing.

phrases.english: And now that you have said
renting does not acquire,
it is a decree because of renting,
and a decree because of lending,
and a decree because of testing.
phrases.notes: This is the sunset sale on ערב שבת from step 10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the proof in step 14 to state the final reasons for the decree.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Selling large animals to a גוי is forbidden because of three concerns: renting, lending, and testing.

steps.title: רב אדא allows selling a donkey through a middleman
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא permitted selling a donkey to a גוי through a Jewish middleman, because none of the three concerns apply to the middleman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא allowed selling a donkey through a middleman. Testing is not a worry, because the donkey does not know the middleman's voice and will not walk for him. Lending and renting are not a worry, because the donkey is not his, so he will not lend or rent it out. Also, he does not want any defect in the animal to be discovered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us a practical ruling of רב אדא. He shows that all three concerns from step 15 disappear when a middleman does the selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testing fails because the animal only responds to its real owner's voice, not the middleman's. Lending and renting fail because the middleman does not own the animal and would not hand it out. He also wants to sell it, so he would not risk a borrower discovering a defect.
steps.confusionAlert: The middleman is a Jew selling someone else's donkey. The point is that he is not the owner, so the animal does not know his voice and he has no reason to lend or rent it out.

phrases.english: Rav Adda permitted
selling a donkey
through a middleman,
if it is because of testing,
it does not know his voice
that it would walk because of him,
phrases.notes: So even if the middleman calls out on שבת, the donkey won't move for him.

phrases.english: and if because of lending and renting,
since it is not his,
he does not lend and does not rent out,
and furthermore,
because he does not want a blemish revealed in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא שְׁרָא לְזַבּוֹנֵי חֲמָרָא אַיְּדָא דְּסַפְסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the three reasons from step 15 and shows a case where none of them apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling a donkey to a גוי through a middleman is permitted, since testing, lending, and renting are not concerns.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks why רב הונא sold a cow to a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא sold a cow to a גוי, and רב חסדא asked him how he could do that, given the ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא sold a certain cow to a גוי. רב חסדא said to him: Why did the Master do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story and sets up a question. רב חסדא wants to know how רב הונא could break the ban we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cow is a large animal, so the decree should forbid selling it to a גוי. The question really works as a challenge, and the answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master (a respectful way to say 'you')

phrases.english: Rav Huna sold
a certain cow to a gentile.
Rav Chisda said to him:
What is the reason the Master acted this way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new practical case that seems to go against the ban stated in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: On what basis רב הונא allowed himself to sell a large animal to a גוי

steps.title: רב הונא: the buyer may want it for slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answered that we can assume the גוי bought the cow to slaughter it, not to work it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Say that he bought it for slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רב חסדא's question. He explains that the sale is fine because the buyer may want the cow for its meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban exists because the animal might be put to work on שבת. If the cow is bought for slaughter, it will not be worked at all, so the concern falls away. רב הונא is willing to rely on this possibility.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Say that he bought it for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's question from step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We may assume the גוי bought the cow for slaughter, so there is no worry that it will be worked on שבת.
